chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Hasan ibn Bint Ilyas from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a boy who breastfeeds once and twice. He said, 'It does not make marriage forbidden.' So I counted for him until I completed ten breastfeedings. He said, 'If they are scattered, then no [it does not make marriage forbidden].' This report also indicates that if they are consecutive, then it does make marriage forbidden.
ai.seo_question: How many breastfeedings are required to make marriage forbidden between a man and a woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific conditions for establishing *radh'* (breastfeeding kinship) by distinguishing between consecutive and scattered feedings. It reflects the scholarly consensus that ten distinct feedings are required to create a permanent mahram relationship, provided they occur within the nursing period, thereby preventing marriage between the wet nurse, the child, and their respective relatives.
